advisory: A finding aid for how a day is put together, and never an authority for what was celebrated. The rules here are transcribed from this repository's own collated publications; the competent particular calendar, a legitimate indult and the competent annual Ordo control an actual celebration. Precedence is one of five decisions, and this layer takes only that one and the orations that follow from it.

abolished.what: The pre-1955 system carries the full commemoration apparatus that the 1955 simplification removed: the Suffragium de omnibus Sanctis, the commemoratio de Cruce, and the seasonal second and third orations of Advent, Lent and the Sundays. These are NOT modelled here. A reader holding a pre-1955 hand missal is holding a book whose commemoration apparatus is richer than this file represents, and the printed second and third collects must be checked against the particular calendar before use.

rules.what: On a duplex I classis day, one commemoration only and it must be privileged.
On a duplex II classis Sunday, one commemoration only, of a duplex II classis feast; omitted if a privileged commemoration is due.
On any other duplex II classis day, exactly one commemoration, privileged or ordinary.
On a lower-grade day, two commemorations.

sung_non_conventual.what: A sung Mass that is not the conventual Mass admits one privileged commemoration and no more.

list.what: A feast or mystery of one divine Person excludes a commemoration of another feast or mystery of the same Person.
The Sunday excludes a commemoration of a feast or mystery of the Lord, and conversely.
A commemoration de Tempore excludes another de Tempore.
A feast of Our Lady or of a saint excludes another commemoration asking the same intercession.

exclusions.not_applied_note: Clauses a and d turn on the identity of a divine Person or of a saint, which this file cannot read off a mass key. They are stated at the step where they would apply and are never applied.

inseparable.what: The mutual commemoration of Ss Peter and Paul is inseparable: two prayers counting as one.

kinds.gloss: An ordinary commemoration is made at every Low Mass and at the conventual Mass, and at no other sung Mass. A sung parish Mass that is not a conventual Mass drops every ordinary commemoration.

order.gloss: The season first, then the order of precedence.

divergences.consequence: Where a primary and a secondary first-class feast of the same dignity occur on the same day, the table reports a tie and the day is marked unsettled. In practice this is rare and usually involves feasts that do not collide in the universal calendar.
divergences.rule_states: Criterion (b) of Divino afflatu distinguishes primary first-class feasts from secondary. A primary first-class feast outranks a secondary one of the same personal dignity.
divergences.this_file_reads: All duplex I classis feasts of the same personal dignity share one row (rows 2-5). The mass index carries no field that distinguishes primary from secondary, so the table cannot separate them.
divergences.what: primary and secondary first-class are merged

divergences.consequence: A duplex II classis feast occurring on a major Sunday is correctly displaced. A duplex I classis feast occurring on a major Sunday correctly displaces it.
divergences.rule_states: Criterion (a) says the higher rite wins "unless a Sunday ... occurs". The exception means major Sundays (Advent, Lent, Passiontide) do not yield to duplex II classis or below, but they do yield to duplex I classis.
divergences.this_file_reads: Major Sundays are at row 6, between duplex I classis (rows 2-5) and duplex II classis (rows 7-10). This is the ordering the exception clause produces: the Sunday yields to duplex I classis but not to anything below.
divergences.what: major Sundays are placed between duplex I classis and duplex II classis

divergences.consequence: Occurrence cases where propriety would separate two same-grade feasts are not resolved here. Concurrence cases where propriety does NOT apply are correctly left as ties, which is the right answer for the wrong reason.
divergences.rule_states: Criterion (e) says a proper feast outranks a common feast of the same grade, in occurrence and in reposition/translation, but NOT in concurrence. So the same two days can be ordered differently depending on the question being asked.
divergences.this_file_reads: A single row number is one order for all questions. This file cannot express criterion (e). Where a proper and common feast of the same grade occur, the table reports a tie and the day is marked unsettled.
divergences.what: criterion (e) propriety of feasts is not expressed in the table

divergences.consequence: A 1962 class III feast that was simplex in the pre-1955 system is placed one row too high, and a class III feast that was duplex minus is placed too low. Both are approximations.
divergences.rule_states: The pre-1955 system distinguishes duplex minus, semiduplex, and simplex below duplex majus. The 1962 system collapsed all three into class III.
divergences.this_file_reads: All 1962 rank III masses are mapped to semiduplex (rows 21-22). Some were duplex minus or simplex in the pre-1955 system, but the mass index does not distinguish them.
divergences.what: 1962 class III maps to semiduplex only

divergences.consequence: An Apostle and a non-Apostle saint of the same grade share a row. Where they occur on the same day, the table reports a tie.
divergences.rule_states: Criterion (c) orders feasts by personal dignity: Lord > BVM > Angels > John Baptist > Joseph > Apostles/Evangelists > other saints.
divergences.this_file_reads: The mass index carries a `kind` field with values christological, marian, and sanctoral. It does not distinguish Angels, John Baptist, Joseph, or Apostles from other saints. All sanctoral feasts of a given grade are placed at the same row (the "other saints" row), regardless of whether they are Apostles or non-Apostles.
divergences.what: personal dignity is approximated from the kind field

fixed_commemoration.gloss: A commemoration attached to a date does not travel with the feast it accompanies.

reposition.why: Reposition answers a perpetual collision, which is a permanent fact about a particular calendar rather than a fact about a date. This repository carries no particular calendar, so nothing here is ever repositioned.

sunday_not_resumed.gloss: An impeded Sunday is gone for that year. It is not moved forward, back, or into the following week.

destination.rule: the next following day that is not duplex I classis or duplex II classis
destination.why_not: The destination depends on the grade of every following day and on the order in which several transferred feasts are placed. This repository does not compute it, and a page that guessed it would be asserting an Ordo result it has not checked. The two destinations the rubric fixes by name are computed, because the rubric states them.

proper_seats.when: 25 March falls between Palm Sunday and the Saturday after Easter inclusive

vigil_dropped.gloss: A vigil is dropped altogether if it falls on a Sunday or on a duplex I classis feast, or if the feast it precedes is itself transferred or reduced to a commemoration.

implied.label: a feria of Advent from 17 to 23 December
implied.note: A semiduplex privileged feria of Advent. An Advent Ember Day falling in this window is also a privileged feria, so the row holds either way.

implied.label: a feria of Advent before 17 December
implied.note: A simplex feria of Advent before 17 December, which yields to any feast and is commemorated if impeded.

implied.label: a day within the octave of the Nativity
a feria after the Epiphany
implied.note: The pre-1955 system celebrates the octaves of Christmas, Easter and Pentecost only, so the days after the Epiphany are ordinary ferias.

implied.label: a feria after Pentecost, in September
implied.note: A September Ember Day is a privileged feria at row 20, but an implied rule fires only where no candidate constitutes the day and none is temporal, so a weekday this rule reaches is one the year file has already shown carries no Ember Day.

not_decided_here: Which calendar binds the celebrant, and every particular, diocesan, religious, patronal, titular and dedication feast that calendar carries. This file carries only the universal calendar.

Whether a duplex I classis feast transferred from an earlier date occupies this one, except at the two proper seats the rubric names.

absolute_cap.gloss: Three orations at most, as in the 1960 code.
absolute_cap.locus: the pre-1955 Missal, Rubricae generales, De Orationibus

ceiling_covers_all.what: The ceiling counts all of them together, not only the commemorations.

conclusions.locus: the pre-1955 Missal, Rubricae generales, De Orationibus
conclusions.what: The Mass's own oration is said under its own conclusion unless another is joined to it; commemorations are said under a second conclusion.

imposed_prayer.locus: the pre-1955 Missal, Rubricae generales, De Orationibus
imposed_prayer.what: The local Ordinary may impose one prayer for a grave and public necessity. Whether one is imposed is a fact about a diocese.

prayer_over_the_people.locus: the pre-1955 Missal, Rubricae generales, De Orationibus
prayer_over_the_people.what: Added after the last postcommunion in Masses of the ferias of Lent and Passiontide, the Sacred Triduum excepted; under its own conclusion; said even when three postcommunions have preceded.

tracked_by.what: as many as there were orations at the beginning of Mass

votive_prayer.locus: the pre-1955 Missal, Rubricae generales, De Orationibus
votive_prayer.what: Any priest may add one at his discretion in read non-conventual Masses on lower-grade days, placed last.

what_counts.locus: the pre-1955 Missal, Rubricae generales, De Orationibus
what_counts.what: the oration of the Mass being celebrated; the orations of a commemorated Office and of any occurring commemoration; other orations the rubrics prescribe; the prayer imposed by the local Ordinary; and the votive prayer.

overrides.locus: DA, Titulus III; the pre-1955 Breviary rubrics
overrides.why: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed yields to an occurring Sunday. The 1962 code states this in the table row itself; the pre-1955 rule states it in the occurrence rubrics of the Breviary, to which the Missal defers.

Two feasts of the same divine Person, or of the same saint, do not commemorate one another: the lower is simply omitted and is not transferred. This file cannot detect that identity from a mass key, so it is stated and never applied.

concurrence.gloss: Concurrence is the meeting of one evening's Vespers, not of two days. It never decides which Mass is said the next morning. Criterion (e) does NOT apply in concurrence, so a proper feast and a common feast of the same grade tie rather than being separated by propriety.

effect.gloss: The Office of lower rank yields: by omission, commemoration, transfer, or reposition. Only duplex I classis feasts may be transferred; others are commemorated or omitted.

precedence.gloss: Five ordered criteria, not a table. This file flattens criteria (a)-(d) into twenty-five numbered rows by grade and personal dignity. Criterion (e) is handled separately. A lower row number wins.
precedence.latin: Ut recte dignoscatur quale ex pluribus Officiis sit praestantius et proinde sive in occurrentia, sive in concurrentia, sive in ordine repositionis aut translationis praeferendum, sequentes praestantiae characteres considerandi sunt: a) Ritus altior; b) Ratio Primarii aut Secundarii; c) Dignitas Personalis; d) Sollemnitas externa; e) Proprietas Festorum.

occurrence.gloss: Occurrence is the meeting of two or more Offices on the same day. Accidental occurrence may lead to transfer; perpetual occurrence may lead to reposition. Criterion (e) — propriety of feasts — applies in occurrence but NOT in concurrence.
occurrence.locus: DA, Titulus III; ADA, Titulus IV

source_advisory: This file is a LINEARIZATION and not the rule itself. The pre-1955 order of precedence is five ordered criteria stated in Divino afflatu (1911) Titulus II — higher rite, primary or secondary, personal dignity, external solemnity, and propriety of the feast — taken in order until one separates two days. It is not a numbered table. This repository's rubrics schema admits only a numbered table, and assembly-model.js picks a winner by comparing one integer. Flattening five criteria into rows produces a file that validates, resolves every day, and decides some of them wrongly: the fifth criterion applies in occurrence and translation but NOT in concurrence, so the same two days can be ordered differently under two questions, and a single row number cannot express that. Every divergence from the rule is recorded in the `divergences` section below. This file states which rubric governs a decision. It does not state what was celebrated anywhere. Precedence is only one of five decisions, and a day resolved here is still subject to the particular calendar of the church, the place, the diocese and the religious institute, to a legitimate indult, and to the competent annual Ordo, which controls. Nothing here is an occurrence witness and nothing here authorises the use of any book.

unsettled.why: This structural recension inherits the base calendar's computation, which emits both the numbered Sunday and the last Sunday in the shared slot and refuses to choose between them. The former citation to "the pre-1955 Breviary rubrics, De Dominica" did not identify a precise, collated locus in a target-edition witness and cannot override that date-scoped refusal. A competent dated Ordo is required.

unsettled.what: two candidates that land on the same row
unsettled.why: The table orders within several rows by properties — primary before secondary, proper before common, Apostles before other saints — that a mass key does not carry. Where two candidates tie, the derivation stops and says the day is not settled here.

unsettled.what: a fixed-date feast inherited as 1962 class III colliding with a day in rows 15 through 23
unsettled.why: The inherited mass index says only that the feast was class III in 1962. In the pre-1955 system it may instead have been duplex minus, semiduplex, or simplex, occupying rows 15 through 23 according to personal dignity. Against another day in that same range, the missing historical grade can change the winner, tie, or commemoration disposition. No target edition source held here identifies that grade, so this occurrence must remain unresolved. A competitor above row 15 defeats every possible grade, and one below row 23 loses to every possible grade; those deterministic cases remain settled.
Where a proper feast and a common feast of the same grade occur on the same day, criterion (e) would separate them in occurrence. This file cannot express that, so the day is marked unsettled.

unsettled.what: DA Titulus III second paragraph and Titulus VI clauses a and d
unsettled.why: All turn on the identity of a divine Person or of a saint, which cannot be read off a mass key. They are stated where they would apply and never applied.

The Suffragium de omnibus Sanctis, the commemoratio de Cruce, and the seasonal orations of Advent, Lent and the Sundays are not modelled here. A page serving pre-1955 from this file shows fewer orations than a pre-1955 hand missal prints.
